title: Adaptive Intake Scorer for Advisory Requests: automated knob recommendations & escalation play
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit optimization requests (batching, prefix/KV caching, quant profiles, routing policy changes) with inconsistent detail and varying SLA urgency. Current manual triage is slow, error-prone, and often routes requests to engineering too early, wasting specialist time.

Proposal: Build an adaptive intake scorer that automatically rates incoming advisory requests across three axes: (1) expected cost-savings, (2) SLA/availability risk, and (3) quality/regression risk. The scorer will combine lightweight static signals (customer tier, model family, sequence length, tokens/day) with optional artifact uploads (sample prompts, eval set, latency traces) to produce: (A) a recommended lane (self-serve, standard advisory, concierge engineering), (B) a first-pass knob recommendation pack (batch size range, cache TTL suggestion, quant profile candidates with estimated accuracy delta, routing fallback policy), and (C) an automated escalation suggestion for e.g., dedicated capacity or canary rollout. The system will provide a short rationale and link to a generated runbook snippet engineers can adopt.

Why this matters: reduces cycle time for enterprise optimization requests, reduces unnecessary engineering cycles, enables predictable SLAs, and provides consistent recommendations to customers and CSEs.
goals: 1) Decrease median time-to-first-recommendation for optimization requests from 4 business days to <24 hours. 2) Reduce inappropriate engineering escalations by 50% in pilot customers. 3) Produce recommendation packs with at least 80% accept rate in trial cohort.
scope_in_scope: automated intake scoring model (rules + lightweight ML)
API/web intake form changes to collect minimal signals and artifacts
dashboard to review scored requests and override recommendations
scope_out_of_scope: full automated deployment of knob changes
large-scale model retraining or eval infra expansion
billing changes or pricing model updates
acceptance_criteria: Scorer deployed behind feature flag and integrated into intake endpoint
Dashboard shows score + recommended lane and knob pack for 90% of incoming pilot requests
Runbook snippets created for recommended changes with clear rollback steps
Pilot with 3 enterprise customers for 4 weeks demonstrating metric improvements vs baseline
implementation_notes: Start with deterministic ruleset for safety-critical signals (SLA tier, model compatibility, explicit 'do not change quant' flags) then add ML scorer to refine priority weights
Quantization recommendations must include an estimated quality delta and an 'evaluate-before-deploy' checklist
Knob suggestion pack will default to conservative values; include explicit safety boundaries (token-level quality thresholds and latency thresholds)
Integrate with Console so CSEs can approve/override and schedule engineering engagements

decisions: Use rule-first scorer then iterate with ML signals after pilot
Provide conservative default knob packs to start (lower batch size upper/lower bounds, cache TTLs >= 1s default, quant candidates limited to 8-bit dynamic and 4-bit experimental)
Escalation lanes: self-serve (email + automated docs), advisory (CSE assisted), concierge (engineering scheduling + dedicated capacity analysis)
tradeoffs: Conservative defaults reduce immediate cost-savings but limit regressions — acceptable for initial rollout
Automating quant suggestions increases speed but raises quality/regression risk; mitigations: require eval sets or holdout prompt checks, staged canary deployments
Building ML scorer early could increase accuracy but delays launch; rule-first gets value earlier
risks: Customers may misinterpret recommendations as guaranteed — include clear language and disclaimers
Insufficient telemetry to estimate quality delta for quant profiles on niche prompts
Overfitting the scorer to pilot customers' workloads; plan to collect diverse signals
